subject: Demo recap + proposed POC: access requirements, success criteria & sprint plan
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@fairwind.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC: access requirements, success criteria & sprint plan

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and the POC proposal so we have alignment before next steps. I kept this intentionally short.

What we showed:
- Redwood hosted API (text gen + streaming) integrated to a small sample ingest pipeline.
- Example inference latency and cost delta when using prefix caching + batching.

Proposed POC (2-week focused sprint):
- Goal: reduce triage time for incoming support tickets by surfacing suggested resolutions and relevant KB links (target: 30% reduction in TTR for triage group).
- Success criteria (measures we will evaluate):
  - Precision@3 of suggested resolutions >= 0.65 on your labeled set
  - Average API tail latency <= 220ms at 25 RPS sustained
  - 99% availability during scheduled window
- Scope: 5k historical tickets sample + production-like synthetic stream for load testing (we'll define a sampling plan).
- Timeline: prep (week 0) -> integration & dataset ingest (week 1) -> evaluation & tuning (week 2) -> readout (end of week 2).
- Owners: Dylan (Redwood PM / POC lead), Ben (SE / integration), Marissa (Customer Success / adoption).

Immediate asks from FairWind:
1) Share a 2–5k sample of ticket data (anonymized) and a short schema doc (fields + typical context length).
2) Confirmation on whether we can provision a short-lived API key and a sandbox SSO for Ben to test auth flows.
3) Any compliance/PSC items you need up front (we can share SOC2 report and limited scope evidence).

Attachments: Redwood_POC_Outline_v1.pdf (contains detailed task list, testcases, and roles).

Suggested next step: if you can confirm dataset availability and a target kickoff week (we have open slots 11/2 or 11/9), we will schedule a 30–45 minute kickoff to assign access and finalize the sprint checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
Email: dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com | Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0147

Dylan —

Appreciate the clear recap. We're excited to move forward. Quick answers and a couple of clarifying Qs: 

- We can provide a 3.5k-ticket anonymized export by EOD Wednesday (will include subject, body, ticket type, and resolution flag). Format will be CSV + JSONL for context windows.
- Sandbox API key / service account: yes, we can provision. Our security team needs to confirm outbound IP allowlist and TTL for keys (~7–14 days preferred).
- Compliance: please send your SOC2 Type II and the short PSC form. We'll triage it through our security team.

Clarifying questions: 
1) For the latency SLA (220ms at 25 RPS), is that measured in our sandbox environment or a Redwood-hosted test harness?
2) Who on your side should our infra/security contact for the allowlist and key provisioning?

We are inclined to aim for the 11/9 kickoff to give our security team time to run the PSC check.

Alex
Product Lead, Search & Assist — FairWind AI
alex.ramos@fairwind.ai | +1 (646) 555-0132

- Infra/security contact: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwoodinference.com) will be the point for IP allowlist and key exchange. He'll send a small access-checklist to speed approvals.

I attached the access checklist and a brief mapping of who owns each task. If that kickoff works, Alex/Priya can confirm and we will send a calendar invite + HubSpot update.

Best,
Dylan
